title: Refinement and base change for fixed normalized proper/open comparisons
statement: Let Lambda be a finite commutative ring. Use bounded-below derived etale module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], exact open extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], proper maps [def-weil-proper-morphism] and open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion]. For every commutative proper/open square fix ordinary natural isomorphisms delta:i_!r_*≅p_*k_! and derived natural isomorphisms gamma:i_!Rr_*≅Rp_*k_!. Assume that for each square k:A→B, i:C→D, r:A→C, p:B→D with k p=r i, delta_F followed by p_*(k_!F→k_*F) and the compositor k_*p_*→(k p)_* equals i_!r_*F→i_*r_*F followed by the compositor r_*i_*→(k p)_*. Assume also that gamma.hom is exactly rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange(delta.hom). Then (1) on a proper refinement fixing the open, gamma, after the canonical identity-direct-image identification, equals properOpenComparison [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]; and (2) for every Cartesian base change the gamma square commutes with the canonical extension-by-zero base-change isomorphisms [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change] and the canonical derived exchange maps [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients], with the exact equation specified in the Lean record. Only equalities of these already supplied maps are asserted; no existence or invertibility claim is part of this conclusion.

proof.text: In the refinement case use [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]. Its construction identifies $V=u^{-1}(j_2(X))$ and its clopen component $s(X)$, with $bs=j_1$, $ps=\mathrm{id}_X$. Restrict the arrow just constructed to $j_2$. Under the restriction isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-derived-open-restriction], the extension-by-zero comparison [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change], and the component restriction [lem-weil-pbc-clopen-section-direct-image], its source and target become $K$. The underived $\delta$ sends a section on $X$ to itself on $s(X)$ and zero on the other component. Thus this restricted arrow is exactly $\theta_{u,K}^{-1}$ from the comparison definition; the resolution map is the canonical derived comparison and does not change that identity on the component. The adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction], descended degreewise since extension by zero and inverse image are exact [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], makes the arrow $j_{2!}K\to Ru_*j_{1!}K$ uniquely determined by this restriction. It is consequently $\alpha_{u,K}$, the adjoint of $\theta_{u,K}^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, specialization to a refinement; comparison definition and its component normalization

proof.text: For base change first work with sheaves. The support inclusions into ordinary direct images in [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition] identify $i_!r_*$ and $p_*k_!$ inside $(ir)_*=(pk)_*$. Its pullback-composition clause says that the two paths consisting of the ordinary comparisons and the extension-by-zero comparisons give the pullback comparison for that same composite morphism. Thus the ordinary version of the required base-change diagram commutes. These are injective inclusions; inverse image preserves them by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Hence equality in the common ordinary direct image is equality in the support subsheaf. The open comparisons $\beta_i,\beta_k$ of [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change] agree with the restrictions $c_k,c_i$ of the ordinary comparisons to the support subsheaves, which the support node calls canonical; we check this for $k$ (the case of $i$ is identical). By [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change], $\beta_k^{-1}$ is the $k_{1!}\dashv k_1^{-1}$ mate of $x=\theta\circ d^{-1}\eta_k:d^{-1}F\to k_1^{-1}a^{-1}k_!F$. Since $\beta_k$ is invertible, $c_k=\beta_k$ iff $c_k\beta_k^{-1}=\mathrm{id}$, iff the adjoint $k_1^{-1}(c_k)\circ x$ is the unit $\eta_{k_1}$ [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. Evaluate on an etale $W\to A_1$: by the presheaf formula [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and the explicit adjunction, $\eta_k,\eta_{k_1}$ are the identity on sections over objects factoring through the open, $\theta$ is the identity on germs, and the ordinary comparison restricts a section along $W\to V\times_BA$, which is $W\to V$ for $V$ factoring through $A$. So both maps send the germ of $s\in F(V)$ to the same germ, and $c_k=\beta_k$. The ordinary-comparison pasting is also the unit/counit mate equation in clauses (1),(2) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] for the module inverse-image adjunctions; all constant-ring pullbacks are the identifications of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact].

proof.text: The assumed derived-unit normalization uniquely identifies every gamma with the rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange map of its delta: use rightDerived_ext, whiskered by the exact open extension. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-cube] to the ordinary support cube from the preceding step. The canonical derived exact-comparison isomorphisms in that theorem are precisely extensionZeroBaseChangeDerivedPlusIso, and the two vertical transformations are derivedBaseChangeMapPlus. This gives the asserted derived cube without assuming that inverse image preserves injectives.
